title: AWS CWI Exam Prep in Chattanooga, TN: 6-Day Course
description: Six-day AWS CWI exam prep for Chattanooga lock, bridge, heavy equipment, auto supplier and nuclear outage welding: Part C code choice, Part B and eligibility.
h1: AWS CWI Exam Preparation in Chattanooga: Six Days for River, Bridge, Heavy Equipment, Automotive and Nuclear Outage Welding Inspectors
html:
The quickest way to understand welding inspection work around Chattanooga is to follow the Tennessee River, the interstates and the plants beside them. On the river, the US Army Corps of Engineers is building a new lock at Chickamauga Dam. On the highways, TDOT has just finished rebuilding the I-75 and I-24 interchange, a job that replaced four bridges. In the plants, Komatsu has built excavators in the city for four decades and Volkswagen has started assembling the 2027 Atlas family. Up the reservoir, TVA's Sequoyah Nuclear Plant runs two reactors that need maintenance and modification work. Every one of those settings produces welds that a qualified person has to accept against a code, a drawing or a contract.

The Atlantis NDT course is six days of preparation for the AWS Certified Welding Inspector (CWI) examination, aimed at welders, fitters, maintenance mechanics, quality technicians, NDT technicians and engineers in Hamilton County, the surrounding Tennessee counties and north Georgia. AWS owns the examination: it writes and administers the test and issues the certification, and each candidate applies to it individually and must personally meet its eligibility and vision rules. The course has no AWS approval or endorsement, and no AWS examination content has ever reached Atlantis. There is no Atlantis classroom in Chattanooga. You can take the six days online at your own pace with an instructor on hand for questions, have them delivered at your employer's plant for a group, or book them one-to-one, online or in person at a location agreed at booking. The day-by-day outline sits on the AWS CWI exam prep page.

The river: a new lock at Chickamauga Dam

The Chickamauga Lock Replacement Project is building a 600-by-100-foot chamber that the Corps says will pass nine barges at a time once it is operating. In November 2026 the Corps' Nashville District held a ribbon cutting marking completion of the upstream approach wall contract, the wall that guides commercial barges and recreational boats into the chamber. Earlier, in May 2026, the Corps ended its separate contract for the lock chamber and said it was exploring every contracting option to finish the remaining chamber work, with the goal of an operational lock by 2028.

Navigation locks pair mass concrete with heavy steel: gates, wall armor and embedded items, along with the machinery that operates them. Steel for Corps work is fabricated and inspected to the contract specifications and the welding codes those specifications invoke, commonly including AWS D1.1 for structural steel. A CWI who knows D1.1 well is useful both in a fabrication shop supplying a project like this and on the site where pieces are fitted and welded in place.

The road: four new bridges at the I-75 and I-24 interchange

TDOT marked the completion of Phase II of its I-75 at I-24 interchange modification in Hamilton County on April 24, 2026, after work that began in 2023. The phase replaced the Moore Road and McBrien Road bridges over I-24 and two I-75 bridges over the railroad, widened I-24 toward Germantown Road and I-75 toward East Brainerd Road, and took every interchange ramp to three lanes. TDOT describes the interchange as fully open to traffic.

Where highway bridges use steel girders, fabrication generally follows AWS D1.5, the Bridge Welding Code, plus the owner's own specifications, with work checked in the shop and connection details checked again during erection. A Chattanooga candidate who wants to work for a bridge fabricator, or for the consultant inspection firms that state agencies hire, should give D1.5 serious thought for Part C. Reading: AWS D1.5.

The plants: excavators, haul trucks and SUVs

Komatsu set up its Chattanooga plant in 1985 as the company's first US manufacturing site, and on July 10, 2026 it marked the 40th anniversary by rolling out its 60,000th excavator, a PC490LC-11. The plant builds medium-size hydraulic excavators, forestry machines and HM400 articulated haul trucks, whose production returned to Chattanooga in 2023, and it runs apprenticeships with Chattanooga State Community College. Machines of this kind are built around large welded structures such as booms, arms, frames and truck bodies. An inspector in that setting checks fit-up, preheat on thick sections, weld size and profile against the drawing, and repair records, usually to the manufacturer's weld standard, with AWS D1.1 as the reference code wherever the drawing calls it up.

Volkswagen began assembling the 2027 Atlas family in Chattanooga in autumn 2026. The company employs more than 4,000 people in the city and has built more than one million Atlas and Atlas Cross Sport vehicles there since the Atlas joined the line in December 2016; ID.4 production at the plant ended in mid-April 2026. Car body joining relies mostly on robots and resistance spot welding, so automotive CWIs tend to work for the suppliers that arc weld frames, brackets and subassemblies, in tooling and fixture shops, and for the maintenance and construction contractors that keep a large assembly plant running.

Sequoyah: welding on an operating nuclear plant

TVA's Sequoyah Nuclear Plant occupies 525 acres beside Chickamauga Reservoir near Soddy-Daisy. Its two pressurized-water reactors support more than 1,000 full-time jobs and are licensed through 2040 and 2041. Refueling and maintenance outages at plants like this include welding on pressure-retaining systems, which at an operating US nuclear plant falls under the plant's ASME Section XI repair and replacement program and the owner's quality assurance procedures. Those documents decide who may examine and accept that work, and a CWI is helpful background rather than a substitute for the qualification the program demands.

Outage and project crews also weld supports, platforms and balance-of-plant piping outside the safety-related systems, and there ASME B31.1 and AWS D1.1 are the familiar references. For the NDT and Level III side of power generation work, see power generation NDT consulting in Chattanooga.

Code books matched to river, road and plant

Part C is the open-book part of the examination, roughly 50 to 65 questions on a code book you choose from the AWS list. The table pairs the options with Chattanooga work and adds one thing to watch for each.

Part C option (exam edition)Chattanooga work it suitsWatch for
AWS D1.1, 2020Heavy equipment fabrication, lock and dam steel, plant structures and platformsThe exam uses the 2020 edition even if your shop has moved to a newer one
AWS D1.5, 2020, with Clause 12TDOT and county bridge steel, bridge repair and rehabilitationFracture-critical member requirements fill a large share of the book
ASME Section IX with B31.1 and B31.3Outage and power plant piping, chemical plant and process pipingThree documents to move between, so practise locating tables quickly
API 1104, 22nd editionGas transmission and distribution pipeline crewsIt covers pipeline welding, not in-plant process piping
AWS D15.1, 2019Railcar and locomotive fabrication or repairUseful only if rail equipment is where you expect to work

For background on the structural code, see AWS D1.1 and D1.1 weld acceptance criteria; for the pipe side, ASME Section IX and ASME B31.1.

Building the application: a seven-step checklist

  1. Find your line in the AWS table. AWS asks for five years of welding-related experience with a high school diploma, four with completed trade or vocational courses such as a welding diploma, two with an associate degree or higher in engineering technology, engineering or physical science, and one with a bachelor's degree in welding engineering or welding technology. AWS decides which line applies and what counts.
  2. Gather proof of education. A diploma, transcript or program completion certificate for the line you are claiming.
  3. Write the experience record job by job. For each employer give dates, the processes and materials, the codes or drawings you worked to, and any inspection, documentation or qualification-test duties, with a supervisor who can confirm them.
  4. Pass the vision test. It is recorded on the AWS visual acuity form; schedule it so it is still current on exam day.
  5. Choose the Part C book. Use the table above and pick for the career, not for the easiest score.
  6. Apply to AWS. In the US the application is due six weeks before the Part B date you want.
  7. Book Parts A and C. Use the eligibility code in the AWS confirmation to schedule the computer-based parts at a Prometric center.

Two hypothetical cases show where Chattanooga records get tricky. A welder who completed a one-year diploma and then spent five years building excavator structures is past the four-year vocational line, provided the employer confirms the dates. A maintenance technician at an assembly plant whose welding is occasional may struggle to show enough welding-related work, and should describe the weld repairs, fabrication jobs and inspection tasks in detail before applying, or look first at the AWS Certified Associate Welding Inspector (CAWI). The CWI requirements guide goes further into what AWS looks for.

Chattanooga State and the AWS Chattanooga Section

Chattanooga State Community College lists a one-year welding technology diploma. Full-time terms run 450 hours in fall and spring and 390 in summer, with day classes at the main campus, the Kimball site and the Dayton welding lab and evening classes at the main campus. The program covers oxyacetylene cutting and welding, shielded metal arc, gas metal arc, flux cored arc and gas tungsten arc welding, plasma arc cutting and carbon arc cutting and gouging, on carbon steel, stainless steel and aluminum. A completed diploma of this kind usually points to the trade or vocational line in the AWS table, subject to AWS's decision. Komatsu's apprenticeship arrangement with the college is one example of local employers pairing schooling with paid shop time, and both halves can belong in an AWS application once they are documented.

The AWS Chattanooga Section is part of District 8, and its invitation to the 2025 District 8 Conference, held at the Catoosa County CCA in Ringgold, Georgia, shows how far across the state line the local welding community reaches. Section meetings are a good place to meet CWIs who can explain how local employers use the credential and, sometimes, to find someone able to verify experience.

Part B: which way to travel

AWS runs Part B, the practical, at its own seminar locations, while Parts A and C are taken by computer at Prometric centers. The AWS list of CWI training locations in late 2026 had no Tennessee entry; Kennesaw, Georgia, and Birmingham, Alabama, were the listed sites in the same corner of the Southeast, with New Orleans, Tampa and Indianapolis further afield. Match the AWS seminar and exam schedule against your work calendar before you apply, and remember that each part needs at least 72 percent. The CWI exam cost calculator helps estimate the trip.

The practical asks 46 questions about tools, specimens and documents that AWS hands you on the day. Practise until fillet weld gauges, a bridge cam gauge, a hi-lo gauge and calipers feel automatic, and get used to judging every measurement against the procedure or acceptance criteria supplied in the exam rather than the ones your plant uses.

Delivering the six days inside a Chattanooga plant

An equipment manufacturer, steel fabricator or maintenance contractor preparing several people can have the course delivered on its own premises under the corporate format. Practical sessions then use the company's welded parts, rejected samples and gauges, and the code work concentrates on the book most of the group will take, D1.1 for fabricators and the ASME option for pipe crews. The employer chooses the weeks, so the course can sit between model changeovers, outage seasons or large shipments. Certification remains personal: each participant applies to AWS, supplies their own vision record and experience evidence, and sits every part under their own name.

Individuals on plant shifts or outage crews usually find the online format easier to fit in. The six days of material can be spread over evenings and days off, beginning with welding symbols and terminology, moving through metallurgy and testing, then into the code book, with the timed practice papers left for the end so the scores mean something. Questions go to the instructor in writing as they come up. Anyone who would rather work through a weak area in conversation can book the one-to-one format, online or in person, and spend the time where the practice scores were lowest.

Where a CWI leads in southeast Tennessee

AWS certification lasts nine years, with renewal applications due at the three-year and six-year marks and recertification at nine years through professional development hours, a new pass of Part B, or the Certified Radiographic Interpreter credential. Many CWIs in the area broaden into NDT, where the employer certifies technicians under its written practice; Atlantis provides training based on ASNT SNT-TC-1A in methods such as VT Level 2, MT Level 2 and UT Level 2, after which the employer certifies. For a grounding in how procedures and welder tests connect, read WPS, PQR and WPQ explained.

Local pages: NDT training in Chattanooga, Practical NDT simulator access from Chattanooga, and CWI exam prep in Nashville, Atlanta and Birmingham.

How to enquire from Chattanooga

Let us know whether you want the corporate, online or one-to-one format, how many candidates there are, which Part C book each intends to take and the Part B window you are aiming for. Employers should add the plant location and the weeks that suit production. If you are unsure whether an experience record will satisfy AWS, summarize it and we will point out the questions to settle with AWS first. Each format is quoted on request, and you will hear back from us within one business day.

faq.q: Is there an Atlantis classroom in Chattanooga?
faq.a: No. There is no Atlantis classroom in Chattanooga. The six days are taken online at your own pace, delivered at an employer's plant for a group, or booked one-to-one online or in person at a location agreed at booking.

faq.q: Can I take Part B in Chattanooga?
faq.a: Not according to the AWS list of CWI training locations in late 2026, which had no Tennessee entry. Kennesaw, Georgia, and Birmingham, Alabama, were the listed sites in the same region. The AWS seminar and exam schedule gives Part B dates.

faq.q: Which Part C code should a heavy equipment welder choose?
faq.a: Usually AWS D1.1, 2020 edition, because equipment manufacturers' weld standards and drawings tend to reference it. Choose the ASME option instead if your future is mostly pressure piping.

faq.q: Does a CWI qualify me for outage work at Sequoyah?
faq.a: Not on its own for safety-related welds. That work falls under the plant's ASME Section XI program and quality assurance procedures, which set the qualification for examination personnel. The CWI is valued background, and it fits balance-of-plant and support welding.

faq.q: I completed the Chattanooga State welding diploma. How much experience must I show?
faq.a: A completed trade or vocational program usually places you on the four-year line of the AWS table. AWS decides whether the program and your work qualify, so keep records of each job and a person who can confirm it.

faq.q: Is there an AWS section in Chattanooga?
faq.a: Yes. The AWS Chattanooga Section is part of District 8. Its notices on sections.aws.org list meetings and events.

faq.q: Can an equipment manufacturer have the course delivered at its plant?
faq.a: Yes. The corporate format brings the six days to your plant for a group and uses your own welded parts and gauges. Every participant still applies to AWS personally.

faq.q: Is the course approved by AWS?
faq.a: No. AWS has not approved or endorsed the course, and Atlantis has no access to AWS examination content. AWS administers the examination and issues the certification.

faq.q: How do I get a quote from Chattanooga?
faq.a: Send the format, the number of candidates and the Part C book through the enquiry link on this page. Quotes are prepared on request, and we reply within one business day.
